definition: Gary Fred Marcus (born 1970) is an American psychologist, cognitive scientist, and author, known for his research on the intersection of cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and artificial intelligence (AI).
details: Advocates hybrid neuro-symbolic AI. Marcus is professor emeritus of psychology and neural science at New York University. In 2014 he founded Geometric Intelligence, a machine learning company later acquired by Uber. His books include The Algebraic Mind, Kluge, The Birth of the Mind, and the New York Times Bestseller Guitar Zero.

explainer.lead: Gary Marcus is an American cognitive scientist, NYU professor emeritus and author, best known as a leading critic of deep learning hype and an advocate of hybrid, neurosymbolic AI.
explainer.knownFor: Arguing that deep learning alone cannot deliver reliable intelligence, in Deep Learning: A Critical Appraisal (2018) and Rebooting AI (2019).

contributions.name: The Algebraic Mind
contributions.detail: His 2001 book argued that neural networks need symbol manipulation to explain human thinking.

contributions.name: Geometric Intelligence
contributions.detail: Founded the NYU-incubated startup that Uber bought in 2016 to create Uber AI Labs.

contributions.name: A critical appraisal
contributions.detail: His 2018 paper listed ten limits of deep learning, from data hunger to poor generalization and lack of reasoning.

contributions.name: Rebooting AI
contributions.detail: Co-wrote with Ernest Davis a 2019 book arguing for common sense, reasoning and knowledge in AI.

contributions.name: Robust.AI and policy
contributions.detail: Co-founded Robust.AI with Rodney Brooks in 2019 and testified to the U.S. Senate on AI oversight in 2023.
